result.target_topic: Remaining performance obligations and revenue recognition timeline
result.target_summary: Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations was $1.1 billion as of January 28, 2024, consisting of contracted license, development, and hardware/software support arrangements. The company expects to recognize approximately 40% of this revenue over the next twelve months, with the remainder thereafter, excluding contracts with a length of one year or less.

This represents a substantial growth in deferred/receivable revenue, indicating a significant expansion in the company's backlog and future revenue visibility. The change in magnitude is material to financial condition and operational expectations.

comparisons.peer_topic: Remaining Performance Obligations Balance and Recognition
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 28, 2024, the aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations under contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year was $85 million, of which $67 million is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose the aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations for contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year, explicitly excluding contracts of one year or less. NVDA reports a significantly larger balance of $1.1 billion compared to AMD's $85 million. NVDA estimates approximately 40% of this balance will be recognized in the next twelve months, whereas AMD specifies $67 million of its $85 million balance is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months (approximately 79%).

sentences.text: Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations, which includes deferred revenue and amounts that will be invoiced and recognized as revenue in future periods, was $1.1 billion as of January 28, 2024.
We expect to recognize approximately 40% of this revenue over the next twelve months and the remainder thereafter.

As of December 28, 2024, the aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations under contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year was $85 million, of which $67 million is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months.
The revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations does not include amounts which have an original expected duration of one year or less.

comparisons.peer_topic: Definition and Scope of Remaining Performance Obligations
comparisons.peer_summary: Remaining performance obligations represent transaction price allocated to unsatisfied or partially unsatisfied performance obligations, including unearned revenue and amounts to be invoiced in future periods, but excluding non-committed software, subscription, or service contracts and contracts with an original duration of one year or less or containing sales-based/usage-based royalties.
comparisons.comparison: NVDA and AVGO both define remaining performance obligations as the transaction price allocated to unsatisfied or partially unsatisfied performance obligations, including unearned revenue and amounts to be invoiced in the future. Both companies explicitly exclude contracts with an original duration of one year or less from this disclosure. AVGO further clarifies exclusions for non-committed software/subscription contracts and sales-based royalties, while NVDA's disclosure focuses on contracted license, development, and support arrangements.

sentences.text: Revenue related to remaining performance obligations represents the contracted license and development arrangements and support for hardware and software.
This excludes revenue related to performance obligations for contracts with a length of one year or less.
Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations represents the transaction price allocated to unsatisfied or partially unsatisfied performance obligations.

Additionally, as a practical expedient, we have not included contracts that have an original duration of one year or less, nor have we included contracts with sales-based or usage-based royalties promised in exchange for a license of IP.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel recognizes net product revenue when performance obligations are satisfied via transfer of control, with substantially all revenue from product sales. Revenue is recognized at shipment or delivery based on shipping terms, even when products include interdependent software components accounted for as a combined performance obligation.
comparisons.comparison: While NVDA discloses specific future revenue amounts tied to remaining performance obligations, Intel describes its general revenue recognition policy where revenue is recognized at the point control transfers (shipment/delivery), implying minimal or no significant remaining performance obligations disclosed separately. Intel notes that substantially all revenue is from product sales, whereas NVDA explicitly quantifies multi-year contract obligations ($1.1 billion).

sentences.text: Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations, which includes deferred revenue and amounts that will be invoiced and recognized as revenue in future periods, was $1.1 billion as of January 28, 2024.
Substantially all of our revenue is derived from product sales.

In accordance with contract terms, the revenue for combined performance obligations and standalone product sales is recognized at the time of product shipment from our facilities or delivery to the customer location, as determined by the agreed-upon shipping terms.

comparisons.peer_topic: Future Performance Obligations and Contract Liabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: As of August 29, 2024, future performance obligations beyond one year totaled $141 million, and customer prepayments and other contract liabilities totaled $907 million, with $766 million classified as other current liabilities.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and Micron (MU) disclose future performance obligations and contract liabilities. However, the scopes and magnitudes differ significantly. NVDA reports $1.1 billion in remaining performance obligations (contracted license, development, and support) for contracts longer than one year. Micron reports $141 million in future performance obligations beyond one year and $907 million in total customer prepayments/contract liabilities. Both exclude short-term contracts (one year or less) from their specific 'remaining performance obligations' metrics, focusing on longer-term commitments.

sentences.text: Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations, which includes deferred revenue and amounts that will be invoiced and recognized as revenue in future periods, was $1.1 billion as of January 28, 2024.
This excludes revenue related to performance obligations for contracts with a length of one year or less.
As of August 29, 2024, our future performance obligations beyond one year were $141 million, which included customer prepayments and other contract liabilities.

Customer prepayments made to secure product supply in future periods and other contract liabilities were $907 million as of August 29, 2024, of which $766 million was reported in other current liabilities and the remainder in other noncurrent liabilities.
